reason: The fibroblast conditions explicitly guide stem-cell descendants toward a supporting-tissue lineage.
expectation: The descendants will enter the fibroblast lineage, providing cells for supporting tissue.

effect: The fibroblast lineage now has collagen messages, suggesting amino acids can supply the building blocks for collagen production.
reaction: The unchanged DNA and newly transcribed messages make the differentiation connection clear.
reason: Amino acids are the building blocks needed to translate the collagen messages into protein.
expectation: The fibroblast-lineage cells will make collagen protein from the amino acids.

effect: The fibroblasts have made procollagen for secretion, so extracellular fluid is the likely next step toward supporting tissue.
reaction: The ER-to-Golgi-to-vesicle sequence clarifies how the protein is prepared for export.
reason: The extracellular fluid contains the space and processing enzymes needed for secreted procollagen.
expectation: The fibroblasts will secrete procollagen, allowing extracellular collagen to form around them.

effect: The fibroblasts have produced an extracellular matrix; combining the living cells with it may complete the supporting tissue.
reaction: The secretion and extracellular assembly sequence makes the matrix's origin clear.
reason: Living fibroblasts together with their collagen-rich matrix are a plausible supporting tissue.
expectation: The living fibroblasts and matrix will form a supporting tissue.

alternatives.reason: This should advance the separate muscle-forming branch, but I can first try to complete the supporting tissue.

effect: The living fibroblasts and their matrix formed supporting tissue, completing that goal; the muscle-forming branch remains.
reaction: The cell–matrix attachments make the tissue more than a bundle of collagen.
reason: The skeletal-muscle conditions explicitly guide the remaining stem-cell descendants toward muscle progenitors.
expectation: The descendants will develop into muscle-forming progenitor cells.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells have RNA messages but remain individual cells; they may need to make muscle proteins next.
reaction: The distinction between committed cells and a mature muscle fibre is clear.
reason: Amino acids supplied protein building blocks for the fibroblast branch and may serve the same role for muscle messages.
expectation: The muscle-lineage cells will use amino acids to make muscle proteins.

effect: The muscle-lineage cells used amino acids to make muscle proteins and became separate myoblasts, completing the chapter without producing mature muscle fibres.
reaction: The distinction between myoblasts and fused mature fibres is useful.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making collagen and assembling living supporting tissue was most worthwhile: the sequence connected gene expression, secretion and extracellular assembly to tissue structure.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second differentiation-and-protein-production sequence was somewhat repetitive, though it made the comparison between lineages useful.

surprise.text: The fibroblasts produced procollagen that was processed and assembled outside the cell, rather than simply releasing finished collagen fibres.

arbitrary.text: Combining the fibroblasts with the matrix after they had already produced it felt a little procedural, although it had the clear purpose of showing cells and matrix as tissue.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the separate myoblasts develop into muscle fibres; the chapter leaves that construction unfinished.
